cells.tense: Right now you're standing in the part of the work that pulls things together, and your hand is on it.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you've kept open — a plan, an invitation, a piece that isn't done — and put ten minutes of it on paper. It gives you a line to stand on instead of a room full of maybe.
cells.core:
You can feel what a thing might turn into before it turns, and it doesn't run you. You still finish what you started, still let something be what it is instead of what it could be, and the people around you know where your pull ends and your push begins. That steadiness is what makes the finishing possible.

This isn't a place to rest. You can see more than the moment needs, and that isn't a problem to close — it's a door. The move from here is naming what you're keeping open and putting it where it can be seen, so the abundance stops living only inside you.

cells.tense: You're already living in a version of this that hasn't happened, bracing for a turn that may not come.
cells.ask: Pick one thing still waiting on a decision and say out loud, to the room or the air, what it is right now. It gives you something finished to hold instead of a future you keep rehearsing.
cells.core:
When this part is working, you gather what's possible and then you let it land — a friend floats a trip, you picture it, and then you book the day. You're saying a thing is done, not almost done.

What's happening instead is that every possible feeling is being assembled and none of them can be written down while you stand ahead of the moment. Holding all of them at once is how you keep from finding out what one of them would cost. The gathering that was meant to serve the making has gone further than any making can use.

cells.tense: Your hand stopped at the doorknob a while back and you're still standing by that door.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you used to bring all the way to done and haven't touched in a while, with nothing after it. It gives you a shape you can look at without having to feel your way into it.
cells.core:
Done right, this is where you finish — a stack of possibilities comes in and you choose, sign, hand it over. People near you could name something you've completed this year, and you could too without hunting for it.

What's been happening instead is that feelings keep arriving and nothing is being gathered from them. The choices sit there and so does the finish. Pushing back in with effort or feeling would only add weight to something already empty — the quieter way is to let your mind be still for a minute and let it sort, which is the opposite of forcing.

cells.tense: The pen is down, and an ending is getting written anyway.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've been treating as a given — the timing, the mood, whatever feels fixed — and cross it out on paper with the words 'mine, chosen' next to it. It gives you back a piece of what you'd been leaving to the day.
cells.core:
On a good day here you gather the possibilities and you know you're the one doing the gathering. You can say why you picked what you picked, and it doesn't need a defense. The result looks less like fate and more like something a person did.

What's running underneath is the same gathering, handed off to something else — the mood, the situation, whoever else is in the room, the way things just are. What you did is real and it's yours, and it keeps getting filed under circumstance. Saying it out loud doesn't add weight; it gives back weight you were already carrying.

The sentence in Status 1 about what the choosing feeds would serve the writer more than the reader, so it names an act instead.
